ch.intro: Where Sentry alarms and other alerts are sent. Set up at least one channel your phone shows instantly — ntfy or Bark — and keep email as an archive.
ch.verified: Delivered — the ntfy server has it
ch.sent_unverified: Sent, but the ntfy server doesn't show it yet
ch.desc.ntfy: Free push app for iPhone and Android. Alarms arrive at top priority with a link to the event.
ch.desc.bark: iPhone only. Alarms ring as Critical Alerts — through silent mode and Do Not Disturb.
ch.desc.telegram: A message from your own bot, with the clip thumbnail when there is one.
ch.desc.email: Slow (minutes), so use it as a record, never as your only alarm.
ch.desc.webhook: POSTs JSON to a URL — for Home Assistant, Node-RED or your own scripts.
ch.desc.apprise: Any of 100+ services Apprise supports (Pushover, Discord, Slack…), comma-separated URLs.
ch.ntfy_new_hint: On a public server the topic name is the password.
ch.ntfy_created: Private topic created — subscribe to it in the ntfy app
ch.ntfy_scan: Install the ntfy app, tap +, and subscribe to this topic — or scan the code: {url}
fleet.heading: Vehicle commands
fleet.intro: Every Tesla built since 2021 — Cybertruck included — only obeys commands signed by a key it has approved. The sign-in TeslaMate uses can read data but cannot sign. These steps give this hub its own key, approved by you, so commands go straight from here to your car; no third-party server sees them. It takes about ten minutes, once.
fleet.sum_pair: Approve the key in the Tesla app
fleet.s1_hint: The private half stays on this machine, readable only by the hub. You will publish just the public half.
fleet.s2: Register a free Tesla developer app
fleet.s2_hint: At developer.tesla.com, create an app for Fleet API. Allowed origin: https://<your domain>. Allowed redirect URI: {redirect}. Grant types: authorization code and client credentials. Scopes: vehicle information, location, commands and charging. Tesla gives every developer account a monthly credit that comfortably covers one personal vehicle — set a billing limit above $0. Then paste the app's details here.
fleet.s3: Publish the public key and register the domain
fleet.s3_hint: Tesla checks that your domain serves the key at {url}. Easiest: a free GitHub Pages site named <you>.github.io — put the downloaded file at that path and add an empty .nojekyll file. Then check it and register.
fleet.s4: Sign in with your Tesla account
fleet.s4_hint: Approve the permissions on Tesla's own page. You'll come back here automatically; if the page you land on doesn't load, copy its whole address and paste it below.
fleet.paste_ph: …or paste the address you landed on
fleet.s5: Approve the key in your car
fleet.s5_hint: On the phone with your Tesla app, scan the code (or open the link) and approve. The car must be online; it asks you to confirm.
fleet.pair_scan: Scan with the phone that has the Tesla app.
fleet.s6_hint: Commands now go from this hub to your car, signed with your own key. Starting over keeps the key, so you won't need to approve it again.
fleet.reset_lead: The developer-app details and sign-in are forgotten. The key itself is kept, so the car's approval stays valid.
sentrycfg.heading: Sentry alerts
sentrycfg.intro: How loudly to tell you about activity around the parked vehicle. An alarm — the alarm going off, something opened while locked, the vehicle being moved — is always delivered. Activity means someone came close.
sentrycfg.home_none: Not set — activity in your own driveway counts as 'away'.
sentrycfg.at_home_desc: You walk past it all day.
sentrycfg.fast_desc: While Sentry Mode is on (the car is awake anyway), check it this often instead of waiting for the logger's 60-second poll. Free; uses no extra battery.
sentrycfg.fleet_note: For instant (1–3 s) alerts that also catch someone pulling a door handle with Sentry off, connect Fleet Telemetry — see docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md.
models.heading: 3D models
models.intro: The car on the home screen. Upload your own .glb for a model line; if it has nodes named door_fl, frunk, tailgate, tonneau…, those parts will open and close with the real car. See static/models/README.md.
models.none: No 3D model — a picture is shown
